chapter_title: The Chapter of the Name of the Fathers
chapter_note: Chapter is dominated by systematic cosmological title→realm (“greatness”) correspondences for multiple divine figures. The only clear later material is the dialogue frame in ¶1–2 and the attribution tag in ¶3; no pastoral drift or NT citation overlay is present.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame: “Once again the enlightener speaks…”; question-introduction apparatus rather than teaching exposition.
Petition/Q&A frame (“We beseech you, our master…”) typical of the Kephalaia’s hagiographic editorial container.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, the Father, who is the first established thing, shall be called ‘the Father of Greatness’. His greatness is the great earth where he lives, he being established in it [...] the essence of the light that swathes all the rich gods and the angels and the dwellings [...] is set over it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution formula: “Then he speaks to his disciples:” (hagiographic/frame layer).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching is an impersonal, systematic mapping internal to the cosmological system: divine title (“Father”) ↔ his ‘greatness’ as a defined cosmic realm (‘great earth’), with hierarchical placement of light/inhabitants. The only late element is the introductory attribution tag.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, they shall call the Third Ambassador ‘father’. His greatness is the light ship of living fire wherein he lives, he being established in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic extension of the same internal correspondence pattern (title ‘father’ ↔ specific cosmic ‘greatness’/dwelling). No institutional application, no citation formulas.

paragraphs.core_text: Once again, Jesus the Splendour shall himself also be called ‘father’. His greatness is the ship of living waters where he lives, he being established in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Uses Jesus the Splendour as a named cosmic entity within the Manichaean hierarchy, not as a Gospel citation; continues the same realm/dwelling correspondence pattern (father-title ↔ ship-realm).
